purpose: Test the user's hypothesis H1 (does the speech model's attribution concentrate on degraded audio?): the focus ratio per clip, grouped by the clip's dominant degradation class, with the overall mean and its 95% CI; a ratio of 1 means no concentration.
filter: rows with non-null focus_ratio_m1 (clips with at least one flagged 20 ms frame); state the number of excluded zero-flag clips in a corner note (column focus_ratio_m1 is NaN for them)

columns.summary: overall mean focus_ratio_m1 with bootstrap 95% CI from Milestone2/AudioXAI/results/summary.json key focus_ratio_m1 (mean, ci)

encodings: strip plot: one column per degradation class (ordered by count, descending), one dot per clip, jittered horizontally, dots colored by correctness (two fixed colors); a per-class mean marker; a horizontal dashed line at 1.0 labelled 'no concentration'; a shaded horizontal band for the overall mean's 95% CI with the mean value and n in a label

axes.x: dominant degradation class of the clip (from AADD)
axes.y: focus ratio (attribution mass in flagged audio ÷ share of audio flagged)

caption: Focus ratio of whisper-tiny's input attribution (gradient × input with SmoothGrad) per test clip, by degradation class. Values near 1 mean the model attends to degraded audio in proportion to its duration, not more; the overall mean's confidence interval includes 1, so hypothesis H1 is refuted.
